name: Gwenfrewi

attributes.attribute: A quasi-historical Welsh heroine of the seventh century.
She escaped a local prince's attempt on her virtue.
The prince decapitated her, and her head rolled into a valley.
A healing well burst forth where her head came to rest.
Her uncle and a minor saint, Beuno restored her head.

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Gwenfrewi was a quasi-historical Welsh heroine of the seventh century. A local prince assaulted her, and she escaped his attempt on her virtue. He pursued her and cut off her head. The head rolled into a valley, where a healing well burst forth. Her uncle Beuno, a minor saint, restored her head, and it knit together leaving a thin scar.

okr.objective: Relate the martyrdom and healing of the Welsh heroine Gwenfrewi.
key_results: A prince beheaded her after she escaped his assault
A healing well burst forth in the valley
Her uncle Beuno restored her head leaving a thin scar
